To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cluster analysis can be used to support the extraction of business object from legacy code, and that the results of cluster analysis are useful for the extraction of classes in legacy code.

(1) cluster analysis is a useful tool to extract classes from legacy code, (2) the results of cluster analysis depend on the choice of variables and methods to be clustered, and (3) a combination of cluster analysis and a simple rule-based method is more effective than cluster analysis on its own.

(1) the use of cluster-analysis is a promising approach to support object-oriented re-design, (2) cluster-analysis has to be applied in several steps, and (3) the use of the resulting cluster-structure is limited to the identification of classes, but cannot be used for the identification of instance variables and methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: Given a legacy software system, how can we extract the business objects it is implementing?
the following questions: • Can cluster analysis support the extraction of business classes from legacy systems?
the problem of extracting object oriented designs from existing software systems, and with the use of clustering techniques in this context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cluster analysis is not suitable for the extraction of business object classes from existing systems.
the cluster analysis technique is a promising tool for the extraction of business object classes.
cluster analysis can be used for finding classes in legacy code, but that the results have to be checked and refined manually by a human designer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can find classes by clustering variables and methods.
cluster analysis can be used as a powerful tool to extract object oriented re-designs.
cluster analysis can be used as an alternative approach for the extraction of business classes in legacy systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cluster analysis can be applied to the problem of finding classes in existing systems, even in systems which have not been designed in an object oriented manner.
the use of cluster analy-sis in this setting is a viable approach to the identification of object-oriented classes.
cluster analysis can be a useful tool in object-oriented re- design of legacy software.
